newsitem.title: RWANDA: Aid agency suspends work in refugee camps in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Aid agency suspends work in refugee camps in Zaire.

text.p: The International Federation of the Red Cross suspended operations in Rwandan refugee camps in Zaire after a landmine blast killed three staff, aid workers said on Monday.
An official of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said it suspended work in camps around the town of Goma on Sunday for a week after the Saturday blast.
The federation said a total of two people were killed and 36 were wounded in a bus destroyed by the mine explosion.
But other aid officials said a total of three people -- all Zaireans -- were killed on the bus carrying Zairean employees.

"We have reports the mine was locally made. Six people required double amputations," said Willa Addis, deputy Rwanda director for Concern, adding that the wounded were treated at Goma central hospital.
The federation said Goma and nearby Rwandan refugee camps were calm on Monday and its staff were in no immediate danger.
The bus, operated by the International Federation of the Red Cross, International Organisation for Migration and U.N. refugee agency, was travelling to Kibumba camp when the mine exploded.
The U.N. refugee agency suspended non-emergency operations in camps around Goma for four days last week because the nearly 750,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees failed to cooperate with a census.
